name: Adobe Photoshop
note: Default bindings hand-authored 2026-09-04; the full shortcut list comes from the ShortcutMapper import in reference/app-shortcuts.json. Every row of Adobe's own "Default keyboard shortcuts" page (helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/using/default-keyboard-shortcuts.html) that the chord grammar can express is added on top of that, with Adobe's Result column as the name and their table heading as the context ("" for the app-wide Popular shortcuts and search rows, "Tools" for Select tools, "Camera Raw dialog" for Use the Camera Raw dialog box, and so on). Adobe retired that URL in 2026 - it now redirects to a stub that only tells you to open Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts - so the tables were read from the last captures of the page itself on the Internet Archive, both of which are listed in sources; the 2022-2025 captures carry an Adobe CMS defect in which 18 of the panel and dialog sections render the Popular shortcuts table instead of their own, so those 18 sections (Panels, Adjustment layers, Animation panel, Brush panel, Clone Source, Color, History, Info, Layer Comps, Paths, Swatches, Puppet Warp, Refine Edge, Filter Gallery, Black-and-White dialog, Transforming selections, Editing paths, Slicing and optimizing) come from the last correct capture and the rest from the last capture before the page was retired. Left out because the grammar cannot express them: every mouse and stylus row (click, double-click, right-click, drag, spacebar-drag, scroll), "hold key while dragging" rows, rows whose key is only a held modifier (Change Cancel to Reset = Alt, Distort = Control), Caps Lock, the opacity/flow "number keys" and "0-9" rows, ranges written as prose (Ctrl + 1 - 5), and the shifted punctuation Adobe prints as a glyph ({ } < > ~), which the grammar has no spelling for - so Increase/Decrease Brush Hardness keep the Shift+] / Shift+[ form already in this file. Rows that list a comma-separated set of keys (the arrow keys for nudging, "Left Arrow, Page Up") are left out rather than guessed at, as are rows where one alternative carries a modifier and the other does not ("Shift + Up Arrow/Down Arrow", "L or Ctrl + ]"), because Adobe's wording does not say whether the modifier distributes. Where a row lists genuine alternatives that all parse ("] / [", "Delete or Backspace") it becomes one action per key with the chord in parentheses after the name. Names already present in this file are not re-added.
